newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-Polish Farm Min ups 97 grain output estimate.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Polish Farm Min ups 97 grain output estimate.

text.p: Poland's Agriculture Ministry on Friday revised upward its 1997 grain output estimates to 24 million tonnes in 1997 from earlier forecast of 23 to 23.5 million as losses from a month-long flood became more apparent.
The ministry also upped its rapeseed output forecast to around 550,000 tonnes, from the previous 400,000 to 450,000 tonnes, its spokeswoman Malgorzata Ksiazek told Reuters.
"According to very preliminary Agriculture Ministry estimates the rapeseed harvest is expected to be around 550,000 tonnes and grain harvest around 24 million tonnes," she said.
Ksiazek added that Agriculture Minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski said in a Friday radio interview that Poland's grain harvest could slightly fall below 24 million, but did not elaborate.
The ministry's previous grain estimate was on July 17, when the extent of the flooding and of damages was not yet known.
The Central Statistical Office (GUS) had finalised Poland's grain production in 1996 at 25.3 million tonnes, higher than earlier estimates around 24.7 million.
It placed last year's rapeseed output at 461,000 tonnes.

Ksiazek said that Poland should import its annual amount of 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes of high-gluten durum wheat in the 1997/98 season and that any further imports needs would only be known after the harvest ends.
"We expect the standard imports of some 400,000-600,000 high-gluten grain and I cannot comment on other (types of grain) imports," Ksiazek said.
"The ministry might decide on whether we need any addtional imports after the harvest results are known and after evaluating the situation on the market," she said.
Poland, whose growing season runs from September to August, does not grow some types of high-gluten grains and therefore imports them every year.
Ksiazek said the ministry may try to install a grain import quota if a need for such a measure arose after this year's harvest but said such a move was only hypothetical.

She said the month-long floods, the worst in centuries, had covered some 130,000 hectares of grain fields, 5,500 hectares of rapeseed fields and more than 9,000 hectares of sugar beets, according to tentative estimates.
July's flooding in Poland submerged a total of 6,600 sq km of land, killed 54 and forced tens thousands out of their homes, causing damage of billions of dollars.
Nearly 1,700 sq kms of Poland were still under water on Friday and some 30,000 people remained displaced, but the floodwaters everywhere were receding.
